requirement: Describe FGCL-4592-060 Amendment 3 as a Phase 3 multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study of roxadustat for anemia in adults with Stage 3-5 chronic kidney disease not receiving dialysis, with at least 52 weeks of treatment and four weeks of post-treatment follow-up.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies the governing amendment, population, design and periods.
The SAP confirms Amendment 3 and the design.

requirement: Under Amendments 2-3, randomize 2:1 to roxadustat or placebo and stratify by screening Hb at most 8 versus above 8 g/dL, cardiovascular/cerebrovascular/thromboembolic history, eGFR below 30 versus at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and US versus ex-US region.

evidence.text: The amended protocol gives the ratio and four strata.
The SAP reproduces the amended randomization.

requirement: Account for the amendment transition: subjects under the original protocol or Amendment 1 could enter QW, BIW or TIW maintenance arms, whereas subjects under Amendments 2-3 use TIW dosing; pool treatment for primary comparisons and identify dose-frequency analyses as legacy supportive analyses.
acceptable_values: original or Amendment 1 QW BIW TIW

evidence.text: The protocol documents the treatment-arm transition and pooled comparisons.
The SAP defines treatment pooling and actual maintenance-frequency presentation.

requirement: For the US submission, define the primary endpoint as each subject's change from baseline Hb to the average central-laboratory Hb over Weeks 28-52, retaining Hb values influenced by rescue therapy in the primary analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the US endpoint and rescue handling.
The SAP confirms its derivation and treatment-policy handling of rescue.

requirement: For ex-US submissions, define response within the first 24 weeks as two consecutive central-laboratory Hb values at least five days apart: Hb at least 11 g/dL plus an increase of at least 1 g/dL when baseline Hb exceeds 8, or an increase of at least 2 g/dL when baseline Hb is at most 8.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the region-specific responder.
The SAP operationalizes values, timing and central-lab use.

requirement: For the ex-US responder estimand, classify subjects who discontinue or receive RBC transfusion, ESA or IV iron on or before the second qualifying Hb visit as nonresponders, and use the second visit to assess rescue exposure.

evidence.text: The SAP states the responder intercurrent-event rule.
The protocol defines response without rescue.

requirement: Derive baseline Hb as the mean of the last four available central-laboratory values before first dose, including the Day-1 predose value, and use prespecified analysis visit windows with the last nonmissing value when multiple measurements map to one visit.
acceptable_values: mean of last four Hb values

evidence.text: The protocol defines baseline Hb.
The SAP defines baseline and visit mapping.

requirement: Define ITT as all randomized subjects analyzed as randomized and use it for US primary efficacy; define ITT1 as pre-Amendment-2 and ITT2 as Amendment-2-or-later subsets.

evidence.text: The SAP defines ITT and amendment subsets.
The protocol assigns ITT to primary efficacy.

requirement: Define FAS as randomized subjects with at least one dose, baseline Hb and at least one postdose Hb, normally analyzed as randomized and used for ex-US primary efficacy; use actual maintenance frequency only for dose-frequency analyses and distinguish FAS1/FAS2 by amendment era.

evidence.text: The SAP defines FAS, attribution and amendment subsets.

requirement: Define PPS as randomized subjects receiving at least eight weeks of treatment with corresponding valid Hb and no prespecified major deviation, finalize exclusions before database lock and unblinding, and use PPS supportively for primary endpoints.

evidence.text: The SAP operationalizes PPS and blinded deviation handling.
The protocol delegates full PPS criteria but says at least 12 weeks, creating an adjudication issue.

requirement: Define safety as all subjects receiving any study medication, analyze according to treatment actually received, and use this population for exposure and all study-specific safety summaries.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the safety set.
The SAP adds actual-treatment attribution.

requirement: Analyze the US primary endpoint with MI ANCOVA comparing pooled roxadustat with pooled placebo, adjusting for continuous baseline Hb and eGFR plus treatment and the remaining randomization strata, then report arm least-squares means, treatment difference, two-sided 95% confidence interval and p-value.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the model, comparison and reporting.
The protocol prespecifies MI ANCOVA.

requirement: Implement the US primary multiple imputation under MAR using 200 datasets: treatment-specific MCMC to create monotone patterns, sequential treatment-specific regression imputation through Week 52, ANCOVA of each completed dataset, and Rubin-rule combination with MIANALYZE.

evidence.text: The SAP supplies the complete primary MI algorithm.

requirement: Analyze the ex-US responder endpoint with a CMH test adjusted for randomization strata, comparing pooled roxadustat with pooled placebo at two-sided alpha 0.05, and report the adjusted odds ratio and 95% interval plus exact arm response-rate and rate-difference intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol prespecifies adjusted CMH inference.
The SAP defines inference and effect estimates.

requirement: Assess US-primary robustness in ITT2, PPS and FAS and with MMRM, pattern-mixture MNAR analyses including last-mean, baseline-carried-forward and jump-to-control variants, and analyses censoring Hb for six weeks or eight weeks during an evaluation period after rescue.

evidence.text: The SAP defines analysis-set, MAR, MNAR and rescue sensitivity analyses.

requirement: Assess ex-US-primary robustness in FAS2, PPS and ITT and with logistic regression using continuous baseline Hb and eGFR plus region and cardiovascular-history strata, with an additional age- and sex-adjusted model.

evidence.text: The SAP defines analysis-set and regression sensitivity analyses.

requirement: Control primary and secondary endpoint multiplicity with the prespecified fixed-sequence hierarchy at familywise two-sided alpha 0.05, proceeding only after rejection; identify comparisons outside the hierarchy as unadjusted or exploratory.

evidence.text: The protocol describes fixed-sequence primary and secondary testing.
The SAP states alpha control and endpoint order.

requirement: Cover the key secondary efficacy domains: Hb maintenance without recent rescue, LDL cholesterol, SF-36 vitality and physical-function scores, mean arterial pressure, rescue and transfusion time-to-event, worsened hypertension, and eGFR decline censored at dialysis or transplant.

evidence.text: The protocol lists and models secondary endpoints.
The SAP gives endpoint derivations and analysis methods.

requirement: Use MMRM for longitudinal continuous secondary endpoints with baseline, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit and applicable strata; try unstructured, heterogeneous Toeplitz, Toeplitz, compound symmetry and AR(1) covariance structures in that convergence order.

evidence.text: The protocol prespecifies MMRM and covariance fallbacks.
The SAP confirms the model and complete fallback sequence.

requirement: Plan at least 450 randomized subjects in a 2:1 ratio, potentially up to 1200 for pooled safety needs; state greater than 99% power for the US Hb endpoint and greater than 95% power for the ex-US responder endpoint using the documented assumptions.

evidence.text: The protocol gives enrollment and power assumptions.
The SAP states the updated US effect assumption and safety-driven cap.

requirement: Summarize exposure, TEAEs through 28 days after last dose, serious and renal events, deaths, discontinuations, laboratory and liver signals, vital signs, ECG including QTcB/QTcF, and excessive hematopoiesis in the safety population, with exposure-adjusted rates where differential follow-up matters.

evidence.text: The protocol defines study-specific safety summaries.
The SAP details safety derivations and outputs.

requirement: Keep adjudicated MACE and other composite cardiovascular safety inference outside the study-specific analysis: describe MACE as death, myocardial infarction or stroke and defer region-specific pooled testing to the separate pooled safety SAP because this individual trial is not powered for it.

evidence.text: The protocol defines MACE and explicitly limits it to pooled program analysis.
The study SAP delegates pooled composites.

requirement: Specify no interim analysis with statistical inference and distinguish ongoing blinded safety and dosing monitoring plus independent DSMB review from formal efficacy testing.

evidence.text: The protocol separates safety review from inferential interim analysis.
The SAP confirms no interim statistical inference.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile protocol-versus-SAP differences in the US power effect assumption and PPS minimum treatment duration, approve amendment-era treatment pooling and hierarchy, and confirm that the SAP release and approval chain predates unblinding despite the later running-header date.

evidence.text: The protocol states a 1 g/dL US effect and at least 12 PPS treatment weeks.
The SAP release field is 2018-09-13 but the running header is 2020; it states a 0.75 g/dL effect and eight PPS weeks.
